title: The Cost of Teaching Operational ML
problem: Operational ML requires skills beyond model development, including infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation—capabilities grounded in HPC and distributed systems but lacking comprehensive educational frameworks.
motivation: Graduate education must equip students with end-to-end ML systems engineering skills, from distributed training to production operations, requiring access to substantial compute resources.
method: Graduate-level course (ML Systems Engineering and Operations) using Chameleon Cloud testbed for hands-on infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation across 186,692 compute instance hours.
key_novelty: First comprehensive cost analysis of operational ML education, documenting compute resource requirements and projecting commercial cloud costs for ML systems course.
contributions: Course design for end-to-end ML systems engineering and operations
186,692 compute instance hours instrumentation and analysis
Empirical resource consumption data across assignments
Commercial cloud cost projection: ~$250/student ($50K for 191 students)
Open educational materials for public reuse
Framework for measuring infrastructure requirements of ML systems education
baselines: Commercial cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure estimated costs)
limitations: Course-specific implementation limits generalizability; Chameleon Cloud infrastructure differs from commercial offerings; cost analysis does not include instructor time or infrastructure overhead.
